subject: Approval: Downsell Guardrails & Early Termination Opt-Out for AtlasCo POC
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.inference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Approval: Downsell Guardrails & Early Termination Opt-Out for AtlasCo POC

Team —

Quick ask for executive/legal sign-off so we can keep momentum with AtlasCo (POC kickoff next week). Summary: AtlasCo agreed to a 3-month POC with a 6-month potential roll if metrics hit. They want a sharp opt-out after month 1 if latency SLOs or cost targets aren’t met. They also asked for a 30% launch discount and the ability to step down commit levels without penalty.

Why this matters: AtlasCo is a strategic probe account in our retail vertical; if they expand, it’s material ARR and a strong reference. But the team needs guardrails so we don't create a precedent that erodes coverage for managed customers.

Proposal (what I want signed off):
- Discount: up to 25% on hosted inference list pricing for the POC term (not 30%).
- Ramp schedule: Month 1 = 25% of committed QPS, Month 2 = 60%, Month 3 = 100% (by end of month).
- Downsell protection: if AtlasCo reduces committed QPS after month 2, they pay at least 75% of the originally committed rate for the remainder of the 6-month term (or we apply credits to recoup onboarding costs).
- Early termination opt-out: allowed only after 30 days with 30-day notice, and requires repayment of onboarding credits (equivalent to the one-time integration credit) OR 50% of remaining committed fees as a termination fee.
- Data/retention: standard retention + audit log access for AtlasCo for 90 days.

Attached: AtlasCo_SOW_v1.pdf and proposed_terms_redline.docx.

Decision requested: Please confirm approval (and any edits) — specifically need Laura or Monica to sign off on the discount and the termination language before I send back to AtlasCo legal. If we can’t get 25% discount and the termination fee, we should push back and keep them at standard PO terms.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni

Subject: Re: Approval: Downsell Guardrails & Early Termination Opt-Out for AtlasCo POC

Vivek —

Thanks for the clear summary and the redline. I reviewed the proposed language and have a few legal edits and a suggested tweak to the commercial terms:

1) Early termination: we should not allow a pure 30-day immediate opt-out without any recoup. Proposed compromise: early termination allowed after 60 days from execution (not 30) OR after 30 days only if customer pays onboarding-credit recoup or 50% of remaining committed fees (explicitly listed). This protects our onboarding amortization.

2) Downsell protection: make the step-down percentages explicit in the SOW and limit the ability to down-sell to once during the POC term to avoid churn abuse. Also include a cap: total allowed reduction <= 40% of original commit across the POC unless mutually agreed.

3) Audit logs/data retention: add a clause that audit log exports are provided on request but require an admin request and up to 10 business days to produce; this limits operational burden.

I've attached legal_redline.docx with inline comments. Two other asks: finance needs to confirm the onboarding credit amount to be recouped, and we need a named SLA metric (p50 latency or 95th percentile?) that AtlasCo agrees to for the opt-out to be triggered.

If the revenue team can accept the 60-day default or guarantee the 50% recoup language, I can push the redline through.

- Monica
Monica Patel
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Quick note — I support Monica’s approach but want to be practical on deal economics. AtlasCo is pushing hard; if we hold them to 60 days we risk losing the POC. My suggestion:

- Approve up to 25% discount (no further).
- Allow a 30-day opt-out only if the customer pays onboarding credit recoup OR 50% of remaining committed fees (as Monica suggests).
- For ramp: make month 1 a lower-min commitment (25%), month 2 escalate to 60%, month 3 to 100%. If they down-sell after month 2, they pay at least 75% of original commit for the remaining term.

This preserves flexibility while protecting revenue. Because the discount is >20% we need Laura’s OK.

—Aditya

Vivek / Team —

I reviewed the thread and authorise moving forward with the following binding conditions:

1) Discount: approved up to 25% for the POC only (no carry to roll unless approved separately).
2) Early termination: allow opt-out after 30 days with 30-day notice PROVIDED that the customer either repays onboarding credits (finance to confirm amount) OR pays 50% of the remaining committed fees as a termination fee. If the customer requests opt-out before 30 days, we deny.
3) Ramp/downsell: accept proposed ramp (M1 25% commit, M2 60%, M3 100%). Downsell after month 2 permitted but limited to one reduction and capped at a 40% total reduction; if they reduce, they pay at least 75% of original committed fees for remainder of the initial 6-month commitment.
4) SLO trigger: the opt-out may only be exercised if AtlasCo breaches a mutually-agreed SLA metric (we should use p95 latency and a clear measurement window). Monica, please add the SLA definition into the SOW redline.

Finance & Legal: please confirm onboarding credit amount and update the SOW/DocuSign. Vivek — once legal updates the redline, send final to AtlasCo and request DocuSign. Use HubSpot deal DL-2026-1287 and route for signature.
